question: Why did the 2018 Tampa Bay Rays start some games with a relief pitcher who threw only an inning or two?
answer: To blunt the cost of facing hitters repeatedly. Batters do better each time they meet the same pitcher in a game, as they read his pitches and he tires. An opener faced the dangerous top of the order once; the usual starter came in later and met those hitters fewer times. Rivals soon copied it.
move: Spend a resource that weakens with use where it counts most.
ask: Where am I spending my best energy early or evenly instead of where it matters most?
reference: Tango, Lichtman & Dolphin, The Book: Playing the Percentages in Baseball, Potomac Books, 2007
